q.t: What is the SI unit of time?
q.e: The second, symbol s, is the SI unit of time. Minutes and hours are larger units built from it.

q.t: How many seconds are there in 1 minute?
q.e: 60 s = 1 min.

q.t: How many minutes are there in 1 hour?
q.e: 60 min = 1 h.

q.t: Speed = ?
q.e: Speed tells how much distance is covered in each unit of time, so divide distance by time.

q.t: What is the SI unit of speed?
q.e: Distance in metres divided by time in seconds gives metres per second.

q.t: The time taken for one complete oscillation of a pendulum is its…
q.e: The time period is the time for one oscillation.

q.t: The position where a pendulum hangs at rest is its…
q.e: At rest the bob hangs straight down — the mean position.

q.t: A sundial tells time using…
q.e: As the Sun moves across the sky, the shadow moves and marks the time.

q.t: Which device measures distance travelled by a vehicle?
q.e: The odometer records distance (km); the speedometer shows speed (km/h).

q.t: Motion along a straight line is called…
q.e: Linear means along a line.

q.t: A car travels 100 km in 2 h. What is its speed in km/h?
q.e: Speed = distance ÷ time = 100 ÷ 2 = 50 km/h.

q.t: A bus moves at 50 km/h for 3 h. How far does it travel (km)?
q.e: Distance = speed × time = 50 × 3 = 150 km.

q.t: A train at 90 km/h covers 360 km. How many hours does it take?
q.e: Time = distance ÷ speed = 360 ÷ 90 = 4 h.

q.t: The time period of a pendulum depends on its…
q.e: Changing the length changes the time period; changing the bob's mass doesn't.

q.t: Two pendulums of the same length but different bob masses. Their time periods are…
q.e: The time period does not depend on mass, so equal lengths give equal periods.

q.t: Why measure 20 oscillations and divide, instead of timing one?
o: It reduces the effect of reaction-time error
q.e: Your start/stop error is spread across many swings, so the answer per swing is more accurate.

q.t: Which way of writing a speed is correct?
q.e: Lowercase units, a space after the number, no full stop. 'sec' is not correct; use s.

q.t: An object covers equal distances in equal intervals of time along a straight line. Its motion is…
q.e: Constant speed in a straight line — equal distances in equal times — is uniform.

q.t: A train speeding up as it leaves a station is in…
q.e: Its speed keeps changing, so it covers unequal distances in equal times.

q.t: Who noticed a swinging church lamp and timed it with his pulse?
q.e: Galileo observed each swing took the same time. Huygens later built the pendulum clock.

q.t: School is 3.6 km away and you reach it in 15 min. What is your speed in m/s?
A cyclist goes 6 km in 30 min. What is the speed in km/h?
q.e: 30 min = ½ h. Speed = 6 ÷ ½ = 12 km/h.

q.t: A pendulum completes 20 oscillations in 40 s. What is its time period (s)?
q.e: Time period = total time ÷ number of oscillations = 40 ÷ 20 = 2 s.

q.t: Distances covered by a car every minute: 1 km, 1 km, 1 km, 1 km. The motion is…
q.e: Equal distances in equal times → uniform.

q.t: Distances every minute: 0.5 km, 1 km, 1.2 km, 0.8 km. The motion is…
q.e: Unequal distances in equal times → speed changing → non-uniform.

q.t: How many minutes did the ghati of the Ghatika-yantra last?
q.e: The sinking bowl took 24 minutes to fill and sink — one ghati.

q.t: How many ghatis made a day?
q.e: A day is 24 h = 1440 min. 1440 ÷ 24 = 60 ghatis.

q.t: Why did the outflow water clock become inaccurate?
o: Water flowed slower as the level dropped
q.e: Less water above the hole means less push, so the flow slowed and the clock fell behind.

q.t: Every clock, from sundial to atomic clock, is built on…
q.e: A repeating process marks equal intervals of time — that is what any clock counts.

q.t: Why is 'speed' in daily life usually average speed?
o: Objects speed up and slow down along the way
q.e: Total distance ÷ total time smooths all the changes into one number.

q.t: A runner covers 400 m in 50 s. What is the average speed in m/s?
A car moves at 20 m/s. How far does it go in 2 minutes (m)?
q.e: 2 min = 120 s. Distance = 20 × 120 = 2400 m.

q.t: A train runs 120 km in the first 2 h and 180 km in the next 3 h. What is its average speed (km/h)?
q.e: Total distance 300 km ÷ total time 5 h = 60 km/h. (Don't average the two speeds — divide totals.)

q.t: Convert 72 km/h to m/s.
A train goes A→B speeding up, B→C steady, C→D slowing. Which part is uniform?
q.e: Only B→C has constant speed.

q.t: You double the mass of a pendulum's bob but keep the length. The time period…
q.e: The time period depends on length, not on mass.

q.t: A pendulum clock is running too slow. What must you change?
q.e: Only the length controls the time period. (A shorter pendulum swings faster.)

q.t: Huygens' early pendulum clocks gained or lost about how much each day?
q.e: About 10 seconds a day. Atomic clocks today lose one second in millions of years.

q.t: Which statement is FALSE?
o: Uniform motion is common in everyday life
q.e: Truly constant speed for long is rare — uniform motion is an idealisation.

q.t: Ravi walks 1.5 km in 15 min; Meena walks 2 km in 25 min. Who is faster?
q.e: Ravi: 1.5 ÷ ¼ h = 6 km/h. Meena: 2 ÷ (5/12) h = 4.8 km/h. Ravi covers more distance per hour.
